_comment: Which local tests run on GitHub Actions, and in which order they are turned on.  Enabling more is a reviewed edit of this file.
The single workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml compiles once per platform ('build' job), uploads the workspace, then runs every
(platform, lane) pair that has an enabled entry as its own job ('test' jobs, in parallel, each on a fresh machine, so lanes cannot
interfere through ports, config directories or temp files).  Test jobs never restore or compile: they run the built test assemblies.
throughBatch: entries whose batch is greater than this are planned but not run.  workflow_dispatch can override it.
Per platform an entry is 'observe' (runs; a failure is reported as a warning and does not fail the job), 'required' (a failure fails
the job) or 'excluded' (does not run; 'reason' says why).  A platform missing from an entry is excluded.  A new batch starts as 'observe';
promote it to 'required' after it has been green on that platform for several runs.
kind: xunit-exe = dotnet <target> [args] (an xUnit v3 test assembly, run directly); msbuild = dotnet msbuild <target> -t:Build.
'project' is built once in the build job (distinct projects only).  'measuredSeconds' is the last measured duration; keep it current when promoting a batch.

'buildFirst' projects are built before everything else on every platform that builds: the host's build writes the host-assembly manifest that lets every add-in trim what the host already ships (without it each add-in carries ~550 MB of copy-local dependencies and AddIns reaches 13 GB); tests/OpenDevelop.IntegrationTests/TESTING.md says the same: build the application first.

'buildArgs' are extra dotnet build arguments for the entry's 'project'; entries that share a project must agree on them.  The integration project is built with -p:BuildIntegrationFixtures=false because its fixture target builds every fixture inside one MSBuild process (Uno.Sdk 6.6.42 then clashes with the already resolved 6.5.31, MSB4240); a lane that needs a fixture lists that fixture's own csproj as an entry 'project' so it builds in its own process.

A lane with 'needsNuGetCache' also downloads the build job's NuGet package cache: the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time, so a lane that starts the IDE (the integration lanes) needs it; the unit lane does not.

'buildLast' projects are built after everything else, with their own 'args' ('{rid}' is the platform's 'rid').  The host is built last with '--runtime <rid> -p:AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath=false', the recipe terminal-cross-platform.yml uses (it builds the Terminal add-in that way, which builds the host project it references as that RID into the same folder) and whose IDE does start on the Windows runner.  Measured on the runner without it: the host's OpenDevelop.deps.json is 166 libraries without a 'PresentationFramework/11.0.0.0' reference entry from the very first host build on, whatever is built afterwards in the default way (a macOS build has 193, with 28 'reference' entries for the LibreWPF assemblies), and the IDE dies at start-up with a FileNotFoundException for PresentationFramework 11.0.0.0.  The build summary records the host deps.json after every build, so the run shows what the RID-specific build changes.
A lane definition holds 'timeoutMinutes', optionally 'needsNuGetCache' (the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time) and optionally 'buildsInLane'.

Profiler and Terminal are entries here; their own workflows (profiler.yml, terminal-cross-platform.yml) were deleted when they were folded in. Only Windows x64 is enabled: the other platforms recorded in platformNotes come back as their own entries.

platformNotes.macos-arm64: Skipped for now: the Terminal journeys fail there on LibreWPF's Display text capability, and profiler.yml's macOS matrix retired with that workflow. Add the platform back to 'platforms' and to entries to re-enable it.
platformNotes.windows-x64: The only enabled platform. The unit lane is required except for base-tests and xamldom-tests-microsoftwpf, which carry one known flaky case each (recorded in their notes). integration-core is excluded until the Windows IDE host can start; see the entries' reason and AGENTS.md.
platformNotes.linux-x64: Not enabled yet: profiler.yml ran the Profiler tests on ubuntu-latest and passed; it comes back as this platform's first entry when the platform is added.

integration-core.note: Kept green while every entry fails for one known host defect, so the lane's failures are warnings instead of a red master; remove 'allowAllFailures' and promote the entries when the host starts.

buildLast.note: Publish the host the way dist.ps1 does: RID-less, framework-dependent. The shipped Windows payload (v5.6.2) has 193 libraries and PresentationFramework.dll both at the app root and under runtimes/win-x64/lib/net10.0/, which is what lets the host resolve the LibreWPF payload by its runtime RID. A '--runtime win-x64' build prunes that tree and the IDE then dies at start-up with FileNotFoundException 11.0.0.0 (measured: 193 DLLs before, 178 after the integration build, no runtimes payload for PresentationFramework).

entries.note: 499 tests (9 skipped) when measured on macOS arm64. On the Windows runner one WinUI Hot Reload case (x86 probe) intermittently reports hr=0x80070490 because the probe can run before the live application applies the change; x64 and ARM64 pass.
141 tests when measured on macOS arm64.
97 tests; the test body is tests/OpenDevelop.XamlDom.Tests.Shared.
Run with dotnet msbuild -t:Build as doc/technotes/addin-sdk.md says; 'dotnet build' fails the same file.

Microsoft's XamlReader is loaded on its own STA thread with a 20-second deadline; on a cold runner the first cases can exceed it and report HANG. One case failed that way on 2026-10-25 while the other 96 passed.

entries.reason: Known-broken on this platform while the Windows IDE host cannot start (FileNotFoundException PresentationFramework 11.0.0.0: the payload is in the host folder but the portable bootstrap returns before preloading it on Windows and the deps manifest registers 167 libraries where the shipped payload has 193). Kept running so the failure stays visible as a warning; flip to 'required' when the LibreWPF SDK fix lands. See AGENTS.md.
